intro: Stalingrad is burning, but the German Sixth Army has finally pushed itself into a trap. As Zhukov, coordinate the blow that will close Operation Uranus: smash the Axis flanks, cut the roads across the Don and Chir, and prevent relief forces from reopening the corridor to Paulus. The Romanian armies are brittle, yet German armour and air power can still punish a careless advance. Break through quickly, preserve your mobile formations for exploitation, and turn the defence of Stalingrad into the encirclement that changes the course of the war.

But we cannot be idle!  A Winter Storm is moving in, and the 3rd and 4th Romanian Armies are squatting along the Chir and Don Rivers.  Also, recon reports that the Italian 8th Army is in the area, and that the 48th Panzer Division is moving East quickly.  Smash these invaders now!

intro: The Stalingrad pocket is sealed, but the wider Axis front on the Don has not yet collapsed. Italian formations, fortified western approaches, and a strongly defended central airfield block the next stage of the counteroffensive. Strike before the enemy can recover from Operation Uranus, destroy the Italian Eighth Army’s cohesion, and open the road toward Millerovo and Rostov. A rapid victory will expand the encirclement and deny Manstein the forces he needs for a relief attempt. Use armour for depth, not merely for the first line, and keep the winter advance moving.

intro: The Chir and Don crossings are heavily guarded, and German aircraft are already moving east to reinforce the threatened sector. Your task is to rupture the river line, seize the bridges, and create the deployment space required for the advance on Rostov. The enemy expects the rivers to slow you long enough for reserves to arrive; prove that expectation fatal. Concentrate artillery on a narrow front, force the crossings under cover, and exploit immediately with mobile units before the defensive network can be rebuilt.

intro: Rostov is the gateway to the Caucasus, but the assault cannot begin until several tactical deployment sites are secured around the city. Reconnaissance reports limited defenders and little air cover—an opportunity that will vanish as soon as the enemy understands your intention. Advance with speed, seize the staging areas intact, and protect the corridors through which the main army must follow. This is a preparation battle in which every turn saved matters: the better your opening position, the less costly the coming struggle for Rostov will be.

intro: Rostov has been reinforced by the Wiking Panzer Division, including heavy Tigers, anti-tank batteries, cavalry, and local air support. The enemy intends to turn the city into a shield for the Caucasus withdrawal and a fortress on the Don. Use reconnaissance to identify the heavy armour, isolate the strongest positions, and attack the city from more than one direction. A frontal rush will burn away your tank strength; combined arms and careful encirclement can instead trap the defenders and open the southern road toward the Crimea.

intro: Sevastopol stands behind coastal guns, prepared urban defences, and incoming airborne reinforcements. Soviet marines, naval forces, aircraft, and paratroopers have already secured footholds around the fortress, but the final assault must be coordinated before Axis help arrives across the Black Sea. Suppress the batteries, protect the landing zones, and break into the city without allowing the defenders to concentrate against a single approach. The capture of Sevastopol will restore a vital base and place the entire Crimean coast within reach.

intro: The road north from Sevastopol appears lightly held, but scattered Axis units and reconnaissance aircraft can still delay the movement toward Odessa. Treat these skirmishes as an operational race: clear the route, preserve fuel and ammunition, and prevent isolated enemy groups from cutting your columns or reporting their strength. Your army must arrive at the next battlefield organised rather than exhausted. A clean pursuit will keep the Black Sea initiative in Soviet hands and ensure that the heavy guns waiting farther west face a concentrated army, not a string of vulnerable detachments.

intro: Odessa is protected by dense anti-tank positions, heavy artillery, Italian naval elements, and two formidable railway guns. The enemy has prepared the coastal approaches to punish armour and delay any direct assault, but Soviet naval gunfire and bomber support are becoming available. Neutralise the long-range batteries, secure the shoreline, and open safe lanes for infantry and tanks to enter the city. This is a combined-arms siege: victory depends on using sea, air, artillery, and ground forces as a single system rather than feeding units into the fortifications piecemeal.

intro: Kursk has been liberated, but German forces are regrouping around Kharkov under experienced commanders and have shot down the aircraft sent to examine their positions. You must advance with incomplete intelligence against a city that has changed hands before and will be defended by armour, artillery, and mobile reserves. Probe carefully, secure the approaches, and avoid exposing your spearheads to a prepared counterstroke. Take Kharkov, break the enemy’s ability to stabilise the front, and clear the way toward the Dnieper operations that will follow.

intro: German and Romanian remnants are holding Kanev to protect the approaches to Kiev and the Dnieper crossings. The visible garrison appears small, but Luftwaffe activity has blinded reconnaissance along the river and hidden whatever reserves wait beyond the city limits. Seize the crossings, eliminate the holdouts, and establish a secure bridgehead before the main battle for Kiev begins. Speed is important, but a careless river assault could leave your formations divided on opposite banks. Take Kanev cleanly and give the armies converging on Kiev a firm southern anchor.

intro: The battle for Kiev is already under way. Konev, Malinovsky, and Vatutin are attacking from the north and centre while your force approaches from the south through uncertain terrain and hostile air cover. Your role is to reinforce the encirclement, seize the southern crossings, and prevent the garrison from escaping or receiving relief. Kiev is too large for a single thrust: isolate districts, coordinate armour with infantry, and keep supply routes across the river open. Liberate the city without allowing the battle to consume the army needed for the advance beyond Ukraine.

intro: With Kiev secured, Romanian resistance around Belgrade threatens the flank and communications of the wider Soviet advance. Enemy tanks, anti-tank guns, and mixed Axis units defend the approaches, while damaged airfields must be captured before your own aviation can operate effectively. Clear the region, seize the bases, and eliminate the possibility of a counterattack from the south. This operation is less spectacular than Berlin, but strategically essential: leave an enemy force behind you and every supply column moving toward Poland will remain in danger.

intro: The armies driving through Poland are waiting for your formation on the south-eastern sector of the front. Luftwaffe patrols have destroyed reconnaissance aircraft, but airborne reinforcements are prepared to seize advanced positions and accelerate the junction. Break through the remaining German screen, protect the drop zones, and connect your force with the neighbouring Soviet armies before the enemy can defeat either element separately. Success will complete the concentration for the final advance to the Oder; delay will give Berlin precious time to fortify its approaches.

intro: The Oder line is the last great operational barrier before Berlin. Enemy troops are scattered around the approaches, city limits are heavily armed, and surprise detachments wait beyond the areas visible to reconnaissance. Secure the crossings, destroy isolated strongpoints, and bring your army into position before the Western Allies can reach the German capital first. The defenders are depleted but still dangerous, especially where anti-tank guns and urban terrain can halt Soviet armour. Open the road to Berlin and preserve enough strength for the battles inside the city.

intro: Berlin is surrounded, but the Luftwaffe and dense anti-aircraft defences have forced Soviet reconnaissance out of the city. The enemy has converted streets, rail yards, government buildings, and hidden arsenals into a layered defensive system whose true strength remains uncertain. Drive into the capital, divide the garrison, and seize the crossings before the defenders can shift reserves between sectors. Expect ambushes, heavy anti-tank fire, and close urban combat. This is not yet the Reichstag assault—it is the battle to make that final objective reachable.

intro: The Reichstag has become the last symbol and one of the strongest fortresses in Berlin. Its defenders possess more ammunition, anti-tank weapons, and heavy artillery than intelligence predicted, while barricades and firing positions have appeared overnight. Reduce the surrounding blocks, isolate the building, and bring infantry and engineers forward under concentrated fire support. Do not squander tanks against hidden guns in the streets. Take the Reichstag, raise the red banner over the centre of German power, and end the European war with a victory worthy of the losses that brought you here.

intro: The guns have barely fallen silent when the alliance begins to fracture. Soviet engineers fortify the eastern sector of Berlin while American, British, and French troops face them across a tense line of demarcation. Orders are to hold ground and avoid opening fire—but an unexpected Allied attack turns occupation into a new battlefield. Stabilise the sector, protect the approaches to East Berlin, and decide whether this clash remains local or becomes the opening shot of another war. Every unit lost now will matter if negotiations fail completely.

I am stepping down from any advice.  It is up to you and General Rokossovsky to consider pushing our so-called allies back to the sea.  If you wish to continue our war, press on General, if not, then stay secure, and wait for the negotiations to end.  The choice is yours General, in my eyes you are the true leader of Russia now.  Whatever your choice Good Luck, and God be with you General.  Further reports will be assigned by another intelligence officer.  Goodbye Zhukov.

intro: Victory over Germany has produced an impossible choice. In this alternate path, Soviet leaders form a new Pact of Steel with former German enemies and Italian forces in order to drive the Western Allies from Europe. British, American, and French armies are retreating toward Dunkirk while German formations secure the northern flank. Commit to the offensive, reorganise a coalition built from yesterday’s enemies, and strike before the evacuation ports can be fortified. The decision taken here abandons historical restraint and opens a campaign of continental conquest.

We have formed a new Pact of Steel with Germany despite both our losses and resentments. It is in Russia's best interests. The Italian armies have also joined on our quest in the expansion westward. The British, American, and French armies have been pushed back to Dunkirk, while our German allies are successfully occupying the Northern Sectors. In addition, the Italian factions are working through Spain. Take Dunkirk, now while it is vulnerable. Then our new Pact of Steel, can push on to Great Britain.

intro: The Western Allies are compressed around Dunkirk, but the port remains their gateway to the English Channel. Soviet, German, and Italian forces must break the siege perimeter, seize an airfield and deployment zone, and prevent another evacuation across the water. Naval and air support are available, yet transport capacity is limited and heavy artillery cannot all be moved forward at once. Secure the coast, destroy the remaining bridgehead, and establish the bases required for an invasion of Britain. Failure here will give the Allies time to rebuild behind the Channel.

We are currently crossing the English Channel encountering some resistence from the British,
American, and French factions. Our new allies have naval and air support, and are currently
transporting units for landing. There are also some paratrooper support in the NW quadrant.
For our full air attack to be employed, it is a priority to annex an airbase, otherwise we will be
sunk in the English channel. There is also a necessary deployment zone to annex. Our units
are getting backed-up, and we don't have the transport capabilities for the bigger heavy
artillery. At this point, it may be wise, to cash in a few units for parachutists or Spenaz. Out.

intro: Operation Nexus carries the new coalition across the English Channel. British, American, and French forces contest the crossing while Soviet and allied transports struggle to deliver armour, artillery, and paratroopers to the southern coast. Capture an airfield immediately or enemy aircraft will turn the beaches and sea lanes into a graveyard. Then seize the deployment zone, widen the lodgement, and prevent the defenders from containing the invasion. The operation is a race between reinforcement and destruction: establish a functioning bridgehead before the Channel closes behind you.

Your force must annex the southern approaches, secure roads and airbases, and prepare the advance on Windsor. The countryside may appear open, but British reserves can use towns, rivers, and narrow routes to delay heavier formations. Keep the landing areas supplied, prevent local counterattacks from reaching the coast, and build a continuous front. A swift southern advance will close the first half of the ring around the British capital.

Exploit identified gaps, secure the airborne landing zones, and break the Windsor defences before British reserves can seal the corridor. The city’s air and ground support remains strong, so every isolated spearhead risks destruction. Take Windsor, connect the encircling forces, and prepare for the final struggle for London.

intro: Britain and France have capitulated, and the war crosses the Atlantic. A Soviet-German naval force, supported by submarines, destroyers, aircraft, and landing troops, approaches the Florida coast before American radar detects the deployment. Enemy destroyers and air units guard the objective, but no reinforcements are expected during the opening assault. Win control of the sea, suppress the coastal defence, and seize the first strategic point intact. This is the campaign’s most audacious leap: if the lodgement fails, the ocean will separate the invaders from every source of heavy reinforcement.

Secure the tactical point, take the airfield, and expand the beachhead before American forces can coordinate a counterattack. Naval gunfire can open the way, but only ground units can hold what has been won. Establish the bridgehead that will carry the war from the Atlantic shore into the American interior.

intro: The Florida landing has succeeded, and the invasion front is moving north. Savannah is strongly fortified, but a captured airbase gives your army access to air and naval support while reinforcements approach from the coast. The city anchors the American southern defence and blocks the route toward Washington. Isolate its fortifications, protect the supply corridor to the beaches, and coordinate bombardment with a deliberate ground assault. Take Savannah before the defenders can turn it into a prolonged siege and allow the northern coalition armies to join the advance inland.

intro: Savannah has fallen and the road toward the American capital is opening. Coalition armies are driving south and west from the Atlantic while your force prepares the next stage of the offensive. American resistance is reorganising around key transport routes, industrial centres, and the approaches to Washington. Keep the columns moving, capture airfields and supply hubs, and prevent the defenders from forming a continuous line. This is the final operational advance of the campaign: every intact unit and every turn saved will strengthen the assault on the capital.

intro: Washington is the final objective of the impossible war that began at Stalingrad and crossed two oceans. The American capital is defended by surviving regular forces, emergency formations, artillery, and whatever air support can still be assembled. Break the outer defensive ring, secure the Potomac crossings, and fight through the government district without allowing your supply line to collapse behind you. The battle is both military and symbolic: victory ends organised resistance and completes the alternate-history conquest. Commit every veteran formation carefully—there will be no campaign beyond Washington in which to replace them.
